California Water Service is a regulated water utility holding company (Cal Water) based in San Jose, California. It supplies drinking water and wastewater services to roughly two million people through about 500,000 connections across California, plus subsidiaries in Washington, New Mexico and Hawaii, founded in 1926. Customers are households, businesses and municipalities, and revenue comes from state-regulated tariffs. It is listed on the NYSE (CWT) as part of California Water Service Group. Local utility brand with limited national consumer visibility, though it has some community and local sports sponsorship history.

Cogito is a Boston-based artificial intelligence company, spun out of MIT, that sells real-time behavioral and emotional-intelligence coaching software for contact-center agents. Its platform analyses voice signals during phone calls and prompts staff on empathy, pace and engagement. Customers are large insurers, health plans and other enterprises with big call-centre operations, paying through software subscriptions. It raised roughly 155 million dollars in venture funding, with the last round in 2023. It was acquired by Verint in 2023. B2B only, with little public brand awareness.

DroneShield is an Australian counter-drone technology company headquartered in Sydney. It makes AI-based detection and defeat systems, including RfPatrol, DroneSentry, DroneGun handheld jammers and the DroneOpsCommand software, which protect military sites, border security, critical infrastructure and events from hostile drones. Customers are defence forces, governments and law enforcement worldwide, and revenue is from hardware sales and software subscriptions, growing sharply since 2022. It is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (DRO). Defence-focused B2B and government brand with modest consumer awareness.

EDP Brasil (EDP Energias do Brasil) is the Brazilian arm of Portugal's EDP group, based in Sao Paulo. It generates, transmits and distributes electricity, running distribution utilities in Espirito Santo and Sao Paulo states plus hydro, wind and solar plants and transmission lines, and also sells energy services. Customers are millions of households, businesses and industrial clients, with revenue from regulated tariffs and power sales. It was listed on the B3 exchange (ENBR3) and majority owned by EDP. Regional utility brand, known locally, with little global consumer visibility.

EngageSmart is a Boston-area provider of cloud software for customer engagement and payments in healthcare and financial services. Its SimplePractice platform serves independent health and wellness practitioners with scheduling, billing and telehealth, while InvoiceCloud provides electronic bill presentment and payment for utilities, local government and insurers. Revenue comes from subscriptions and payment-processing fees from many thousands of small practices and organisations. It listed on the NYSE (ESMT) in 2021 and was taken private by Vista Equity Partners in 2024. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

Fenix Games is a Web3 and blockchain gaming publisher based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It acquires and operates mobile and online games and uses blockchain technology and digital assets within them, aiming to build a portfolio of titles and studios. Customers are gamers, and revenue would come from in-game purchases and token or asset sales. It raised about 150 million dollars in funding, most recently in 2022. Gaming brand with niche crypto-gaming audience and limited wider consumer awareness.

Firestorm Labs is a San Diego defence technology company that builds modular, mission-adaptable unmanned aircraft and develops systems for rapid, distributed manufacturing of drones, using 3D-printed airframes made near the point of use. Customers are the US Department of Defense, the Air Force and allied military buyers, and revenue comes from government contracts and drone system sales. It has raised roughly 150 million dollars, with the latest round in 2026. B2B and defence-focused, with little public brand awareness.

Glarner Kantonalbank is the cantonal bank of the canton of Glarus in eastern Switzerland, headquartered in Glarus. It offers retail and commercial banking, mortgages, savings, pension and retirement planning, and investment and wealth services to local households, small businesses and public bodies, earning mostly net interest income and fees. It is majority owned by the canton and its shares trade on the SIX Swiss Exchange. A small regional bank with strong local presence and limited national brand awareness.

InfoBionic is a Texas-based digital health company, headquartered in Burleson, whose platform provides virtual telemetry and remote cardiac monitoring. Its MoMe wearable monitor and cloud software use AI-assisted analytics to detect arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation and send alerts to clinicians. Customers are hospitals, cardiology practices and independent diagnostic testing facilities, and revenue comes from device and monitoring service fees. It has raised roughly 150 million dollars from investors. B2B medical brand with little consumer awareness.

Justworks is a New York-based cloud HR platform and professional employer organisation for small businesses. It offers payroll, benefits administration, compliance, time tracking and HR support, acting as co-employer for companies that typically have under a few hundred staff. Revenue comes from per-employee monthly fees and benefits and insurance revenue. Founded in 2012, it raised about 160 million dollars from investors including Bain Capital Ventures, Thrive Capital and Redpoint. A known small-business brand with modest advertising presence, but not a mass consumer name.

Kitchen United is a Pasadena, California operator of shared commercial kitchens and delivery-only restaurant facilities. It rents turnkey kitchen space and equipment, plus technology and delivery integration, so restaurant brands can serve online-order and delivery customers without building full restaurants. Customers include national and regional restaurant chains and independent concepts, and it raised about 150 million dollars from investors including Google Ventures. It ran sites in several US cities but scaled back sharply after the pandemic delivery boom. Little consumer brand awareness.

Matsmart is a Stockholm-based online retailer of surplus food and consumer products, buying overstock and short-dated goods from manufacturers and selling them at discounted prices direct to households. It operated in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark and Germany and raised about 158 million dollars of funding. It sells through its own website and app, so revenue is from product sales to consumers. Discount e-commerce consumer brand with moderate awareness in the Nordics.

Mirae Asset Capital Markets India is the Indian securities and investment arm of South Korea's Mirae Asset Financial Group, based in Mumbai. It offers broking, wealth and portfolio services, investment banking, research and distribution for retail, high-net-worth and institutional clients, earning commissions, advisory and trading fees. Parent Mirae Asset is one of Asia's largest independent financial groups. Moderate brand profile among Indian investors, and mainly known in finance circles rather than among mass consumers.

Paper Boat is an Indian beverage brand owned by Hector Beverages, based in Bengaluru. It makes traditional-style Indian drinks and snacks such as aamras, jaljeera, aam panna, coconut water and nimbu pani, sold in tetra packs through retailers across India and exported to several countries. Customers are mass consumers, and revenue comes from packaged-goods sales. It has raised about 150 million dollars from investors including Sequoia, Chryscapital and Sofina. A well-known consumer food and beverage brand with strong nostalgia-led marketing in India.

Parag Milk Foods is an Indian dairy company based in Manchar, Maharashtra, producing milk, cheese, ghee, butter, whey protein and dairy snacks. Its consumer brands include Gowardhan, Go Cheese, Pride of Cows, Avvatar sports nutrition and Topp Up, sold to households, retailers and food-service buyers across India with some exports. Its large processing plants supply milk collected from many farmers. The company is listed on India's NSE and BSE (PARAGMILK). Strong regional consumer dairy brand with significant retail visibility.

Rockhopper Exploration is an oil and gas exploration and development company, headquartered in the UK and listed on London's AIM (RKH). It is best known for the Sea Lion oil discovery in the North Falkland Basin and, later, a stake in Italy's Ombrina Mare project, which led to a long arbitration case against Italy. Revenue is project and asset based, from partners and potential awards. It has raised around 160 million dollars over time. B2B energy company with very little consumer brand awareness.

Securiti is a San Jose-based data security and privacy software company founded in 2019. Its Data Command Center platform uses AI to discover sensitive data across clouds and SaaS apps, and automates governance, privacy compliance, access controls and AI-security. Customers are large enterprises and regulated organisations, paying subscription fees. It raised about 156 million dollars from investors including Mayfield and General Catalyst, and was acquired by Veeam in a roughly 1.7 billion dollar deal announced in 2025. B2B software with little public brand awareness.

Steadfast Group is Australia's largest general insurance broker network and underwriting agency group, headquartered in Sydney. It supports hundreds of franchised broker firms, owns brokerages and underwriting agencies and provides technology and services, placing commercial and personal policies for business and household clients. Revenue comes from commissions, fees and underwriting agency income, with operations also in New Zealand, Singapore, Ireland and the UK. It is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (SDF). Strong in the broker trade, with modest consumer awareness.

Strike Energy is an Australian oil and gas exploration and production company based in Thebarton, South Australia, listed on the ASX (STX). Its main assets are the West Erregulla gas field in the Perth Basin of Western Australia, developed with Mitsui and Warrego, and the Southern Cooper Basin gas and oil interests, with a stake in a urea and renewable fuels project. Customers are domestic gas buyers and industrial users. B2B energy producer with limited consumer awareness.

Thrive Financial, Inc. is a Richmond, Virginia fintech that connects banks, merchants and consumers through technology for payments and financial services, working with partner banks on mobile and card-based offerings. It raised 150 million dollars in funding. Customers are financial institutions, merchants and their consumers, with revenue likely from platform and transaction fees. Largely a B2B financial technology brand with limited consumer awareness.

Unrivaled is a professional women's 3-on-3 basketball league founded by WNBA stars Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, with a first season in early 2025 in Miami at Wayfair Arena. It features top WNBA and international players, offseason competition, player ownership stakes and competitive salaries, and earns from media rights, sponsors, tickets and merchandise. It raised about 150 million dollars from investors, with the most recent funding in 2026. Growing sports brand with strong social media reach and appeal to female and younger audiences.

Waaree Energy Storage Systems is the lithium battery and energy storage arm of India's Waaree Group, headquartered in Mumbai and a sister company of Waaree Energies, the solar panel maker. It provides battery packs and energy storage systems for utilities, commercial and industrial users, telecom and residential customers, earning from product sales and projects. It reportedly raised about 13 billion rupees. The parent group is a very large Indian solar brand, though the storage company itself is a B2B player with limited consumer awareness.

XINYI Information Technology Ltd is a Shanghai-based startup described as an IoT chip company. Its Crunchbase industries are in communication hardware and related semiconductor fields, and it has raised about 1.02 billion Chinese yuan in funding. It is headquartered in Shanghai, China, and presumably sells integrated circuits and hardware to device makers rather than to consumers. Product lines, customers and ownership are not confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

AmBank Group (AmBank) is a Malaysian banking and financial services group headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, listed on Bursa Malaysia (AMBANK). It offers retail, business and corporate banking, Islamic banking, investment banking, insurance (AmGeneral, AmMetLife) and fund management to individuals, companies and institutions. Japanese partner Sumitomo Mitsui Banking and Australia's ANZ have been shareholders, and the Azman Hashim family is the largest holder. The input shows a Sao Paulo location, which looks like a data error. Known consumer bank in Malaysia with a sizable branch network.

Chabaidao is a Chinese freshly made tea drink chain, whose name means "tea Baidao", headquartered in Chengdu with an overseas address in Singapore in the data. It sells fruit tea, milk tea and light-latte drinks through thousands of franchised and directly operated stores across China, aimed at young consumers at lower to mid-range prices. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2025. Widely visible consumer brand in China's tea chain market with active celebrity and sports-themed marketing.

HUB Cyber Security is a Tel Aviv-based Israeli cyber security company, founded as a confidential computing and secure cloud provider and expanded through acquisitions such as Comsec, Ayala and Cyberlock to offer cyber consulting, cyber defence and secure computing. Customers are governments, defence bodies, banks and corporations, earning from projects, products and services. It listed on Nasdaq (HUBC) through a SPAC merger with Mount Rainier Acquisition in 2023. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Mamaearth is an Indian personal care brand, the flagship of Honasa Consumer, based in Gurugram. It sells toxin-free baby products, shampoos, face washes, skin creams and body care under Mamaearth, The Derma Co, Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's and BBlunt, through its website, marketplaces such as Amazon and Nykaa, and offline retailers. Founded in 2016 by Varun and Ghazal Alagh, it listed on India's NSE and BSE in 2023 (HONASA). Strong consumer brand across India with heavy advertising and celebrity campaigns.

Napco Security Technologies is a manufacturer of electronic security, access control and alarm communicator products, based in Amityville, New York. Its offerings include Gemini and Prima alarm panels, StarLink cellular and IP communicators, Marks locks, Continental access control systems and recurring-revenue cloud services. It sells through distributors to security installers and dealers who serve homes and commercial buildings. It is listed on Nasdaq (NSSC). B2B brand, known in the trade, with little public consumer awareness.

Tryg is Denmark's largest non-life insurer, headquartered in Ballerup near Copenhagen, with operations across Denmark, Norway and Sweden. It sells motor, home, accident, property, commercial and pet insurance to private customers, small businesses and large corporates under the Tryg brand, plus Trygg-Hansa in Sweden after its 2021 acquisition of RSA Scandinavia. Gross premiums are some 30 billion Danish kroner. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (TRYG), with the TryghedsGruppen foundation as main holder. Familiar Nordic consumer brand and long-time sponsor.

Allot is an Israeli communications software company based in Hod Hasharon that provides network intelligence, security and monetisation solutions. Its products include Allot NetworkSecure, DNS and endpoint security services for mobile and broadband operators, plus traffic management and analytics. Customers are telecom operators and enterprises worldwide, who pay through software, subscription and service fees. It is listed on Nasdaq (ALLT) and founded in 1996. B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Cello World is an Indian consumer products company based in Mumbai, known for Cello branded writing instruments (pens), plastic housewares, bottles, storage and containers, and for glassware, opalware and mouldings. It sells in India and exports to many countries through a large retail and distribution network. It listed on India's NSE and BSE in 2023. Well-established household brand in India with wide retail reach and cricket-related marketing history.

Copart is a US online vehicle auction company, headquartered in Dallas, Texas. It runs auctions of salvage and clean-title cars, trucks and motorcycles through websites and about 200 physical yards in the US, Canada, UK, Germany, Spain, Brazil, UAE and other countries. Sellers are insurers, dealers, fleets and charities, and buyers include rebuilders, dealers and export buyers; Copart earns seller and buyer fees. Annual revenue is several billion dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (CPRT). B2B-oriented brand with limited general consumer awareness.

Ependion, formerly Beijer Electronics Group, is a Swedish industrial technology group based in Malmo. It makes industrial communication and automation products through brands such as Westermo, Korenix, Beijer Electronics and Neuron, including data communication, robust networking and human-machine interfaces for railways, energy, transport and manufacturing. Customers are industrial machine builders and infrastructure operators. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (EPEN). B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Evaxion Biotech is a Danish clinical-stage biotechnology company in Horsholm, Denmark, using AI platforms (AI-Immunology, PIONEER and RAVEN) to design vaccines and immunotherapies. Its pipeline covers personalised cancer vaccines, such as EVX-01, and bacterial and viral vaccines, and it has partnerships and licensing agreements with firms such as MSD and the Gates Foundation. Revenue is mainly from collaborations and grants. It is listed on Nasdaq (EVAX). Drug-development company with no consumer brand.

Financial Products Group (FPG) is a Tokyo-based Japanese financial services company that arranges and manages leasing-based investment products, primarily aircraft and ship leasing funds for investors, plus fund management, real-estate-related financing and investments. Customers are wealthy individuals and corporate investors, and revenue comes from fees and fund investments. It is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (Prime market, 7148). A finance-industry brand with modest public profile in Japan.

Green Dot is a US financial technology and bank holding company, previously based in Pasadena and now in Provo, Utah. It issues prepaid and debit cards, runs the GO2bank consumer account and provides banking-as-a-service for partners such as Walmart, Apple Pay Cash and gig platforms, earning interchange, fees and interest. Customers are underbanked consumers and fintech and retail partners. It is listed on the NYSE (GDOT) and has been in a 2025 deal to split its businesses. Known to consumers via retail card racks.

Grid Dynamics is a digital engineering and software services firm headquartered in San Ramon, California, with large delivery teams in Eastern Europe, Poland, India and other locations. It builds cloud, data, AI and e-commerce platforms for retailers, consumer goods makers, finance, technology and healthcare clients, working on a time-and-materials or project basis, with revenue of roughly 350 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (GDYN). B2B services firm with little consumer awareness.

Infcurion Group is a Tokyo-based Japanese financial technology company and software developer, providing financial IT services such as core systems, payments and digital banking development to banks, securities firms and other financial institutions. It reportedly raised about 14.4 billion yen. It is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. B2B finance-systems brand with little consumer awareness, so sponsorship fit is limited to corporate hospitality.

Kitron is a Norwegian electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company in Asker, Norway, producing printed circuit board assemblies, cables, box-build products and mechanical products for customers in defence and aerospace, energy and telecoms, industrial, medical and vehicle sectors. It has factories in Norway, Sweden, Lithuania, Germany, Poland, the US and China, with annual sales of roughly 8 billion Norwegian kroner. It is listed on Euronext Oslo Bors (KIT). B2B contract manufacturer with little consumer awareness.

Kuwait Financial Centre, known as Markaz, is an asset management and investment banking company in Kuwait City. It runs funds, real estate and private equity investments, brokerage, research and advisory services for Gulf institutions, high-net-worth and retail investors, earning management fees and investment returns. It was founded in 1974 and is listed on Boursa Kuwait (MARKAZ). Respected regional finance brand, with modest public visibility outside investor circles.

LIC Housing Finance is an Indian housing finance company, based in Mumbai and promoted by Life Insurance Corporation of India, which is its largest shareholder. It provides home loans, plot loans, home improvement and loans against property to individuals and developers, funded by bonds and bank borrowings, with loan assets of about 2.8 trillion rupees and a nationwide branch network. It is listed on India's NSE and BSE (LICHSGFIN). Well-known finance brand in India through its LIC association.

Masan High-Tech Materials is a Vietnamese resource company, based in Ho Chi Minh City and a subsidiary of Masan Group. It owns the Nui Phao tungsten, fluorspar, bismuth and copper mine and processes advanced materials after acquiring H.C. Starck's tungsten business (now Masan Tungsten), selling to industrial and technology buyers worldwide. It is a leading non-Chinese tungsten supplier. It is listed on Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (MSR). B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

Minerva Foods is a South American meat processor headquartered in Barretos, Sao Paulo, Brazil. It slaughters and sells beef, as well as lamb, pork and by-products, with plants across Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Colombia, and exports to more than 100 countries. Customers are retailers, food service and importers, and it is one of the region's largest beef exporters. It is listed on Brazil's B3 exchange (BEEF3), controlled by the Vilela de Queiroz family. Mostly a B2B brand with limited consumer visibility.

Phunware is an Austin, Texas software company providing mobile application and location-based technology. Its products include a Multiscreen-as-a-Service platform, mobile app development, in-app advertising and data tools, and a stake in Lyte, formerly for blockchain and lightbulb activity. Customers are brands, venues, hospitality, sports and political clients, and revenue is licensing, services and advertising. It is listed on Nasdaq (PHUN). Small B2B technology brand with low consumer awareness.

Potbelly Sandwich Works is a US fast-casual sandwich chain headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. It serves toasted sandwiches, salads, soups and milkshakes in roughly 450 shops, mostly company-owned plus franchised stores across the US, with delivery and catering. Founded in 1977, it earns money from food sales and franchise fees. It is listed on Nasdaq (PBPB). Recognisable consumer restaurant brand with regional strength in the Midwest and with moderate national awareness.

Shoper is a Polish e-commerce software company in Krakow providing a hosted online store platform for small and medium retailers. Merchants use it to build webshops, manage products and orders, payments, delivery and marketing, paying monthly subscription fees, with additional revenue from Shoper Payments and add-ons. It has tens of thousands of stores and is part of the Shoper capital group, including Shoplo. It is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (SHO). B2B brand with moderate recognition among Polish retailers.

Solutions 30 SE is a Luxembourg-incorporated technical services company (headquarters shown as Getafe, Spain in the data) that provides installation and maintenance of telecom, energy, IT and digital infrastructure, for example fibre rollout, smart meters and EV chargers, in countries including France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Belgium and Spain. Customers are telecom and utility firms and large corporates. It is listed on Euronext Paris and has faced accounting and audit scrutiny in recent years. B2B services brand with little consumer awareness.

TechWing is a South Korean electronics company in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi-do, that makes semiconductor test equipment, specifically test handlers and related automation hardware for memory chip makers such as Samsung and SK hynix. Revenue comes from equipment sales and service to chipmakers. It is listed on the Korean KOSDAQ market and has reported capital or funding of about 118 billion won. B2B industrial technology brand with no consumer visibility.

TheStreet is a New York-based financial news and information company, founded in 1996 by Jim Cramer. It publishes market news, stock analysis, investing advice and personal-finance content via TheStreet.com and sells premium subscriptions and ad-supported content. It was listed on Nasdaq (TST) until it was acquired by TheMaven (now Arena Group) in 2019, and it later sold its Ratings business and was further divested. Known name among US retail investors.

Viewtrix Technology is a company based in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, listed among public companies in the data. Its Crunchbase industries include developer platform and electronics, suggesting it makes electronic hardware or components and related development tools for device makers. It has raised roughly 132 million dollars in funding. Its products, customers and listing venue are not confirmed here, so no further detail can be given. Likely a B2B technology supplier with no known consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Vita Coco is a New York-based coconut water company, selling Vita Coco coconut water in cartons and bottles, plus coconut oil, Runa tea and the Ever & Ever and PWR LIFT brands. It sources coconuts from the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Brazil and elsewhere, and sells through grocery, convenience and club retailers in the US and about 40 other countries, with annual revenue of roughly 500 million dollars. Founded in 2004, it is listed on Nasdaq (COCO). Widely recognised consumer beverage brand with a history of celebrity and sports sponsorship.

Cint is a Stockholm-based software company running a global digital market research exchange. Its platform connects research buyers, such as agencies, brands and consultancies, with a panel network of over 300 million respondents in more than 150 countries, who complete surveys for rewards. Cint earns transaction-based fees on survey and audience sales, and acquired Lucid in 2021 and Dynata assets in 2024. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (CINT). B2B insights brand with almost no consumer awareness.

Don't Nod Entertainment is a French video game developer and publisher based in Paris, founded in 2008. It is known for narrative adventures including Life Is Strange, Remember Me, Vampyr, Tell Me Why, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden and Lost Records: Bloom & Rage. Revenue comes from game sales to players on PC and consoles, plus publishing deals with partners such as Square Enix. The company is listed on Euronext Growth Paris (ALDNE). Gaming brand with strong recognition among narrative-game fans.

Exyn Technologies is a Philadelphia-based robotics company that builds autonomy software and sensor systems allowing drones and ground robots to operate without GPS or remote pilots in underground mines, tunnels, warehouses and industrial sites. Its ExynAero and ExynPak products create 3D maps and inspection data for mining, energy and construction customers, who pay for systems and software subscriptions. It raised about 60 million dollars, including funding from Sandvik. B2B industrial technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Flow Capital is a Toronto-based alternative asset manager and specialty finance company, providing non-dilutive revenue-based and royalty-style financing to growth-stage technology companies, mainly in North America. It earns interest, royalties and fees, and also manages funds for outside investors. It has raised around 70 million dollars. It is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (FW). Small financial brand with low profile beyond Canadian tech finance.

H100 Group is a Stockholm-based Swedish holding company in healthcare and life sciences, with a focus on generative AI, digital health and medical device businesses acquired as subsidiaries. It is listed on the Nasdaq First North market in Sweden and has raised around 764 million Swedish kronor in funding. Customers are healthcare providers and patients, with revenue from clinics and technology services. Small and little known, with limited consumer awareness.

Heartseed is a Tokyo-based Japanese regenerative medicine company spun out of Keio University, developing cardiac cell therapies made from iPS cells, notably HS-001 for severe heart failure, and partnered with Novo Nordisk, which has global rights outside Japan. Revenue is from collaboration payments and milestones, as it has no marketed products. It raised about 86 million dollars before listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth market in 2024. Research-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

Jagatjit Industries is an Indian alcoholic beverage and spirits maker based in New Delhi, founded in 1944. It produces whisky, rum, brandy and vodka under brands such as Aristocrat, Imperial Gold, 100 Pipers (licensed) and Hunter, and runs bottling and a distillery in Punjab, plus ethanol and malt operations. Customers are Indian state retail systems, distributors and some export markets. It is listed on India's NSE and BSE (JAGAJITIND). Established regional spirits brand, but alcohol advertising limits.

poLight is a Norwegian technology company in Horten (Tensberg), Vestfold, making TLens, a tuneable optical lens built on piezoelectric MEMS technology, which gives autofocus to small cameras in wearables, barcode scanners, medical devices and other products. Customers are device and module makers, and revenue is product sales and development fees. It is listed on Euronext Oslo Bors (PLT) and has raised about 76 million dollars. B2B component brand with little consumer awareness.

REGO Payment Architectures is a Blue Bell, Pennsylvania fintech developing Mazoola, a family digital wallet and payments app and platform that lets children and teens under parental control spend and save safely, sold through banks and credit unions as a white-label offering. It has raised roughly 60 million dollars and trades on the US OTC market (RPMT). The product is aimed at families and financial institutions. Small company with limited consumer brand awareness.

1847 Holdings is a New York-based holding company that acquires small businesses, owning companies such as Kyle's Custom Wood Shop (cabinetry), Wolo Manufacturing (vehicle horns), High Mountain Door & Trim, Sierra Millwork and ICU Eyewear. Revenue comes from sales of products and services in consumer and building trades. It has raised around 38 million dollars and is listed on NYSE American (EFSH). Small cap with limited consumer awareness, although ICU Eyewear carries a retail presence.

Bruton, shown as Hamilton, Bermuda, is described as an energy and financial business with listed status in the data. The Crunchbase industries span energy, finance and financial services, and it has raised about 50 million dollars. Its exact operations, products and ownership are not confirmed here, so it should be treated as a small, little-known holding or investment vehicle. No consumer profile is known. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Citizens Development Business Finance (CDB) is a Sri Lankan non-bank financial institution based in Colombo, providing SME and micro loans, leasing, vehicle finance, gold loans, fixed deposits and business finance to individual and business customers. Revenue is net interest income and fees through a nationwide branch network. It is listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange (CDB, formerly CITW/CDB). Known regional finance brand in Sri Lanka, although small by global standards.

CoinShares is a European digital asset investment firm based in St Helier, Jersey, which runs exchange-traded products (including Physical Bitcoin, listed in Europe), actively managed funds, a trading and capital markets desk and staking services. Customers are institutional and retail investors, and revenue is management fees and trading income, with assets under management of several billion dollars. It listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and added a US Nasdaq listing in 2025 (CSHR). Known in crypto finance circles, with growing profile.

Cyient is an Indian engineering, technology and data analytics services company based in Hyderabad, founded in 1991 as Infotech Enterprises. It provides design, engineering, geospatial, digital and manufacturing services to customers in aerospace and defence, rail, utilities, communications, medical technology and automotive, with operations in about 20 countries and revenue of around 700 million dollars. It is listed on India's NSE and BSE (CYIENT). B2B services brand, little consumer awareness.

E2E Networks is an Indian cloud computing company based in New Delhi, providing GPU and CPU cloud infrastructure, web hosting and AI training and inference services via its TIR platform, including NVIDIA H100/H200 capacity, for startups, enterprises and government AI projects. Revenue comes from usage and subscription fees. It is listed on India's NSE (E2E) and was reported to raise major funding from a Tata-linked group in 2025. B2B tech brand with little consumer awareness.

Ebix is a US software and services company, previously based in Johns Creek, Georgia, serving insurance, financial and travel customers with insurance exchange software, claims, payments and remittances (including EbixCash in India), and e-learning. Revenue was around 1 billion dollars before it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2023 and sold its businesses to Eraaya Lifespaces. It was listed on Nasdaq (EBIX) until delisted. B2B brand with little public awareness.

EEMS Italia is an Italian semiconductor testing and electronics services company based in Milan, historically part of the Eems group and listed in the Italian market. It provided assembly, test and related semiconductor services to chipmakers, and the data also lists semiconductor and electronics as its industries. Reported funding is about 35 million. It is a B2B industrial supplier with no consumer profile and little public information about its current activity.

EFG Hermes is an Egyptian investment bank and financial services group, headquartered in Cairo (6th of October City), with operations across the Middle East, Africa and Frontier markets. It provides investment banking, securities brokerage, asset management, private equity and, through EFG Holding, consumer finance units such as valU (buy-now-pay-later), Tanmeyah and Aman. Customers are institutions, high-net-worth and retail clients. Listed on the Egyptian Exchange (HRHO) and the London Stock Exchange. Well known in regional finance with growing consumer fintech exposure.

Hammond Power Solutions is a Canadian manufacturer of dry-type transformers and power conversion equipment, based in Guelph, Ontario, and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (HPS.A). Its products include general purpose, medium-voltage, harmonic mitigation and specialty transformers, sold through electrical distributors and directly to industrial, commercial, utility and data centre customers in North America, Mexico and India. Revenue is around 600 million Canadian dollars. B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness.

ICTK is a South Korean semiconductor security company in Seoul that develops physically unclonable function (PUF) chips and authentication technology for IoT devices, vehicles and payment cards. Its technology is used to give each device a unique, unforgeable identity. It has raised about 55 million dollars and is listed on the KOSDAQ. Customers are chipmakers and device makers, so it is a B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Incolease is an Egyptian non-bank financial company based in Giza that offers vehicle and equipment leasing and finance, with financing worth around 2 billion Egyptian pounds listed in the data. Customers are businesses and individuals, with revenue from lease and finance income. The company is listed in Egypt. Small, regional finance brand with limited consumer awareness. Strong national energy company, with some sponsorship.

Suning Sports is the sports business arm of Suning Holdings Group, based in Nanjing, Jiangsu, which owned Inter Milan football club (through Suning Holdings, until 2024), Jiangsu FC (which closed in 2021) and sports media business PP Sports. It deals in sports rights, media, events and club ownership. Recorded funding is about 600 million dollars. Privately held, with high profile in football, though financial problems led to Inter's change of ownership to Oaktree in 2024.

West Shore is a Boston-based real estate investment firm that acquires, develops and manages property, including residential and lifestyle assets, for institutional and private investors, with recorded funding of about 600 million dollars. It earns rent, fees and sale proceeds. Its portfolio, scale and ownership are not confirmed here. B2B real estate brand with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Ytech is a Miami, Florida real estate development company providing development and redevelopment of residential and commercial property, in a market with a lot of recent condominium and luxury building. Recorded funding is about 565 million dollars. Its projects, ownership and scale are not confirmed here. Privately held, as far as is known, with local profile only and no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Basrah Gas Company (BGC) is an Iraqi joint venture based in Zubair, Basra, that captures and processes associated gas from the Rumaila, West Qurna 1 and Zubair oilfields, producing dry gas for power plants, LPG and condensate. It is owned by South Gas Company (Iraq, 51 percent), Shell (44 percent) and Mitsubishi (5 percent). It supplies domestic power generation and exports products. Recorded funding is about 500 million dollars. B2B energy brand with a low profile outside Iraq.

Dhanani Group is a Sugar Land, Texas family business that became one of the largest US quick-service restaurant franchisees, operating hundreds of Wendy's, Popeyes, Carl's Jr. and Burger King outlets, along with real estate and fuel stations. It was founded by Shamoon Dhanani in Houston. Recorded funding is about 500 million dollars. Privately held. Customers are consumers via the franchised brands, with the Dhanani name mostly known within the franchising industry.

Elkem is a Norwegian advanced materials company based in Oslo, founded in 1904, producing silicones, silicon metal, ferrosilicon, carbon solutions and microsilica from plants in Norway, China, France and North America, using hydropower. Customers are chemical, construction, electronics, automotive and energy companies in the world. Revenue is about 35 billion Norwegian kroner. It is majority owned by China National Bluestar (CNCG), and is listed on Euronext Oslo Bors (ELK). B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

Energocom is the Moldovan state-owned electricity supplier and trader based in Durlesti, near Chisinau, set up to import power and sell to distribution companies and large customers in Moldova, especially after the end of old supply arrangements with a power plant in Transnistria. It is a government enterprise. Recorded funding is about 430 million. A B2B energy brand known to the energy trade in Moldova, with limited consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Lodestone Energy is a New Zealand renewable energy company based in Takapuna, Auckland, which builds and develops sustainable power projects, mainly solar farms, in Australia and New Zealand. It earns income from selling electricity and project development. Recorded funding is about 520 million dollars. Privately held. B2B energy brand with a low consumer profile. Scale and ownership are not confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Marqeta is an Oakland, California card issuing and payment processing platform that lets businesses launch and manage virtual and physical cards, through modern APIs. Its customers include Block (Cash App), Uber, DoorDash, Klarna, Affirm and Brex. Revenue comes from processing fees, with total payment volume above 250 billion dollars. Founded in 2010 by Jason Gardner, it is listed on Nasdaq (MQ). B2B infrastructure brand with little consumer awareness.

Orazul Energy is a Peruvian power generator based in Lima, owning hydroelectric plants including Cañon del Pato, Carhuaquero, Cahua and Gallito Ciego, plus some thermal capacity, and selling electricity to distributors and large industrial clients. It was formed when Actis acquired Duke Energy's Latin American generation assets in 2016. Recorded funding is about 480 million dollars. B2B power producer with little public brand awareness, so consumer sponsorship appeal is low.

Patria Investments is a Cayman Islands-registered alternative asset manager focused on Latin America, with operations in Sao Paulo, offering private equity, infrastructure, real estate, credit and public equities funds to institutional and wealthy investors. It manages more than 40 billion dollars and was formed in 1994, with Blackstone and later Itau as investors. It is listed on Nasdaq (PAX) since 2021. Financial brand known to investors, with no consumer profile.

Six Nations Rugby is the company that runs the Six Nations Championship, the annual men's, women's and under-20 rugby union tournament between England, France, Ireland, Italy, Scotland and Wales, based in London. It sells broadcast rights, title sponsorship (Guinness), commercial partners and tickets, with CVC Capital Partners having bought a stake of about 14 percent in 2021. Revenue is hundreds of millions. High-profile sports property with a large TV audience; an official title and partner sales process is established.

SoundCloud is a Berlin-based audio streaming platform and music community, founded in 2007, where artists upload and share music, podcasts and audio, and listeners stream it free or through subscription plans (SoundCloud Go). It reportedly has over 300 million tracks and 175 million monthly users, and earns revenue from subscriptions, advertising and artist services (SoundCloud for Artists). It has raised about 540 million dollars from investors and is privately held after a 2024 profit. Strong brand among emerging artists and young listeners.

Ziply Fiber is a Kirkland, Washington fibre broadband provider, formerly Frontier's northwest operations, which sells fibre internet, phone and TV to homes and businesses in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana and neighbouring states. It was owned by WaveDivision Capital before being bought by BCE (Bell Canada) in 2025 in a deal worth about 5 billion Canadian dollars. Revenue is subscription based. Regional consumer broadband brand with growing recognition in the Northwest US.

Bank of Valletta (BOV) is Malta's largest bank, based in Valletta, with a national branch network and retail, corporate, wealth and insurance business, including BOV Life. It serves households, businesses and government in Malta, with total assets of about 10 billion euros. It is listed on the Malta Stock Exchange (BOV) with the Maltese government as a minority shareholder. Very well known in Malta, and a leading sponsor of sport, culture and events there.

Coor Service Management is a Nordic facility management company, headquartered in Solna near Stockholm, offering cleaning, property maintenance, catering, security, reception and workplace services to companies and public bodies in Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland. It has about 10,000 employees and revenue of roughly 11 billion Swedish kronor. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (COOR). B2B services brand, with limited consumer awareness.

Dianwoda is a Hangzhou-based on-demand delivery company in China, offering crowd-sourced last-mile and same-city delivery for restaurants, retailers and e-commerce, using a network of riders who take orders through its app. It was backed by Alibaba and other investors and raised about 450 million dollars, and later became part of Alibaba's local services ecosystem alongside Ele.me. B2B logistics brand with little consumer awareness.

Elektroprivreda Srbije (EPS) is Serbia's state-owned national electricity utility, based in Belgrade, generating power mainly from lignite and hydro plants, mining coal, and supplying electricity to millions of households and businesses nationwide. It employs around 30,000 people. Revenue comes from electricity sales and it is wholly owned by the Serbian government. Everyone in Serbia knows the brand, and EPS has sponsored sport and cultural events locally.

Exotec is a French robotics and logistics company, based in Lille area (Wasquehal), best known for the Skypod automated warehouse system, in which robots climb racks to fetch goods. Customers are retailers and distributors such as Decathlon, Gap, Uniqlo and Carrefour. Founded in 2015, it became France's first industrial robotics unicorn in 2022, and has raised about 447 million dollars. Privately held, with backing from 83North, Iris Capital and Dassault Systemes. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Goetel is a German telecommunications company based in Gottingen, Lower Saxony, providing broadband internet and fibre connectivity, along with network hardware and services. It is a regional carrier that serves homes and businesses in its area, with recorded funding of about 345 million. Its scale and ownership are not confirmed here. Regional telecom brand with limited national consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Guitar Center is a US retailer of musical instruments, based in Westlake Village, California, with about 300 Guitar Center stores and Music & Arts stores, selling guitars, drums, keyboards, DJ gear and pro audio, online and via lessons. Customers are musicians and hobbyists. Revenue is around 2.3 billion dollars. It is privately held by Ares Management after a restructuring in 2020, having been taken private by Bain Capital in 2007. Very recognisable music retail brand in the US.

MX Technologies is a Lehi, Utah fintech data platform, formerly MX, which connects financial institutions and fintechs through account aggregation, data enhancement, budgeting tools and open banking APIs. Customers are banks, credit unions and fintech apps, serving tens of millions of end users. It has raised about 450 million dollars from investors including TCV, and is privately held. B2B brand, with little consumer awareness because it runs inside other firms' apps.

OKEA is a Norwegian oil and gas producer based in Trondheim, listed on Euronext Oslo Bors (OKEA), operating fields on the Norwegian continental shelf such as Brage, Draugen and Gjoa, and developing Statfjord Satellites. It sells oil and gas to the market, with production of about 35,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Recorded funding is about 425 million dollars. B2B energy brand, with no consumer awareness.

OMS Group is a Malaysian multinational telecommunications engineering company based in Shah Alam, Selangor, offering independent network services such as design, installation, optimisation and maintenance for mobile operators and tower companies. Recorded funding is about 400 million dollars. Its footprint and ownership are not confirmed here. B2B services brand with little consumer awareness, so any sponsorship appeal would come from corporate hospitality only. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Silk Road Group is a Georgian investment holding company based in Tbilisi, founded in 1998, with interests in real estate (the Silk Road development in Tbilisi), energy, banking, hospitality and logistics, and known for its role in the planned Anaklia deep sea port project on the Black Sea. It is privately owned by founder Giorgi Ramishvili. Recorded funding is about 400 million dollars. Known across Georgia and the Caucasus, with a reasonable corporate profile.

TMX Finance, the parent of TitleMax, is a Savannah, Georgia consumer finance company that makes title loans secured by a customer's vehicle through about 1,000 TitleMax, TitleBucks and InstaLoan stores in the US. Customers are consumers who have limited credit access. Revenue is interest and fees. It is privately held, owned by the Tracy Young family, with recorded funding of about 450 million dollars. Known brand, though controversial for its high interest rates.

ASK Chemicals is a German foundry chemicals company based in Hilden, North Rhine-Westphalia, supplying binders, coatings, feeders and filters for metal casting, with plants worldwide. Customers are automotive, machinery and engine foundries. It is privately held, owned by private equity. Recorded funding is about 315 million. B2B industrial chemicals brand with no consumer awareness, so any sponsorship rationale would be corporate hospitality or recruitment.

Aspen Bridging is a UK specialist lender based in Solihull, West Midlands, offering short-term bridging loans, development finance and commercial mortgages to property investors, developers and landlords. It earns interest and fees on secured loans, and recorded funding is about 250 million pounds, probably debt facilities. Privately held. B2B finance brand with moderate recognition among property intermediaries and no consumer profile. Scale and ownership are not confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Exail Technologies is a French high-technology group based in Paris, formed in 2022 when iXblue merged with ECA Group. It makes navigation systems, inertial sensors, maritime autonomous vessels and underwater drones, robotics and photonic components for defence, civil marine, space and aviation customers. It has around 2,000 employees and revenue of about 400 million euros. It is listed on Euronext Paris (EXA). B2B and defence brand, known in naval circles and with little consumer awareness.

FormFactor is a Livermore, California maker of advanced semiconductor wafer probe cards, analytical probes, probe stations, cryogenic systems and thermal test equipment used by chipmakers to test integrated circuits at the wafer level. Customers include memory and logic manufacturers such as SK hynix, Samsung and Intel, and revenue is around 700 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (FORM). B2B semiconductor equipment brand with no consumer awareness, so sponsorship appeal is limited to corporate hospitality.

Harmoney is New Zealand's largest online personal lending platform, based in Auckland and also active in Australia. It offers unsecured personal loans funded by retail investors and institutions, with a credit risk model that prices loans for individual borrowers. Revenue comes from loan interest and fees. It began as a peer-to-peer lender in 2014 and is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (HMY). Recognised consumer finance brand in New Zealand, with a mainstream advertising presence.

Hero FinCorp is an Indian non-banking financial company based in New Delhi, part of the Hero Group (Munjal family), offering two-wheeler loans, personal loans, used car loans, loans against property, supply chain finance and consumer durable loans to retail customers and small businesses. It has a nationwide branch network and a large loan book, partly serving Hero MotoCorp dealers and buyers. Recorded funding is about 27 billion rupees. Well known in India through its Hero group connection, with limited direct consumer advertising.

Hydrow is a Boston-based fitness technology company selling a connected indoor rowing machine with a large screen, plus the Hydrow Wave and subscription fitness content filmed on real rivers with Olympic rowers. Customers are home exercisers who pay a one-off equipment price and a monthly membership. Founded in 2017 by Bruce Smith, it has raised about 367 million dollars and sponsors rowing events. Privately held. Recognised consumer fitness brand in the US with a strong rowing community.

IQE is a Cardiff, Wales-based global maker of compound semiconductor wafers using epitaxy, supplying materials used in 5G handsets, wireless chips, photonics, infrared and VCSELs for 3D sensing, with customers including chip makers such as Skyworks, Qorvo and Broadcom. Revenue is about 150 million pounds with sites in the UK, US, Taiwan and Singapore. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM (IQE). B2B technology brand, with no consumer awareness.

La Colombe Coffee Roasters is a Philadelphia-founded coffee roaster and beverage company, shown with a Los Angeles office, known for its Draft Latte canned cold coffee, bottled cold brew, whole bean coffee and cafes across US cities. Founded in 1994 by Todd Carmichael and JP Iberti, it was acquired by Chobani in 2023 for about 900 million dollars, having earlier received an investment from Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya. Wide US retail and cafe presence. Strong consumer brand.

Lightstorm is a Singapore-based telecom infrastructure company that builds and operates subsea cable systems and fibre networks across Asia, including the Bay of Bengal Gateway cable, and sells capacity, cloud-connectivity and managed network services to carriers, content providers and enterprises. It is a relatively new company, with recorded funding of about 32 billion in an Asian currency shown without a clear symbol. B2B telecom brand with no consumer profile. Ownership details are not confirmed here.

Mayville Engineering Company (MEC) is a Wisconsin-based contract manufacturer of metal fabricated and assembled components, with plants across the US Midwest, serving commercial vehicle, construction, powersports, military, agriculture and other industrial customers such as Polaris and Deere. It also provides coating, assembly and engineering services. Revenue is around 550 million dollars. It listed on the NYSE (MEC) in 2019. B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness.

Noveon Magnetics is a San Marcos, Texas manufacturer of sintered neodymium (NdFeB) rare earth permanent magnets, the largest in the US, with recycling technology that produces EcoFlux magnets from recycled materials. Customers are electric vehicle, motors, wind, defence and robotics companies. Recorded funding is about 344 million dollars. Privately held, and it has gained attention in US supply chain independence from China. B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness.

NUBURU is a Colorado-based laser technology company, in Centennial near Denver, developing high-power blue laser systems for welding, additive manufacturing and processing of copper and other materials in batteries, electronics, aerospace and automotive. It sells industrial lasers to manufacturers. It listed on NYSE American (BURU) via a SPAC merger in 2023, with recorded funding of about 327 million dollars, and has since faced financial pressure and a business pivot toward defence. B2B technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Oviva is a Swiss digital health company based in Zurich, running a platform and coaching service for diabetes, obesity and nutrition. Dietitians and coaches guide patients through an app, and the service is reimbursed by health insurers in Germany, the UK, France, Switzerland and other countries, as well as employers. Founded in 2014, it has raised about 347 million dollars, backed by Eight Roads and Tikehau. Privately held. Healthcare brand known to clinicians and insurers, with growing awareness among patients.

WHP Global is a New York-based brand management company that acquires and operates consumer brands, including Anne Klein, Joe's Jeans, Toys R Us and Express, licensing them to retailers and manufacturers worldwide. Founded in 2012 by Yehuda Shmidman, it is owned by private equity investors and has recorded funding of about 375 million dollars. Revenue comes from royalties and licensing. B2B licensor behind several well-known consumer names, with sports and retail marketing partnerships.

ATN International is a Salem, Massachusetts telecommunications holding company that operates wireless, broadband, fibre and wireline services in the US, Guyana and the Caribbean, with brands such as Commnet, Choice, Viya (US Virgin Islands) and GTT. Customers are consumers, businesses and carriers, with revenue of about 750 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (ATNI). Regional telecom brand with local consumer visibility but little wider profile.

Bluebird Network is a Kansas City, Missouri-based fibre-optic network operator that provides data transport, dark fibre, internet, voice and colocation services to carriers, businesses, schools and governments across Missouri, Illinois, Kansas and neighbouring states. It owns thousands of route miles of fibre. Recorded funding is about 285 million dollars. Privately held. B2B telecom brand with low public awareness outside the carrier community.

Bracell is a Brazilian pulp and paper company based in Sao Paulo, part of Royal Golden Eagle (RGE), controlled by Sukanto Tanoto. It produces eucalyptus pulp (including specialty cellulose for textiles) at mills in Bahia and Sao Paulo, and a new pulp mill in Mato Grosso do Sul, with investments of about 6 billion dollars. Customers are paper and tissue makers and textile producers worldwide. Privately held. B2B commodity brand with no consumer awareness.

Fullcryo is a company based in Beijing, China, described in Crunchbase as a cryogenic equipment manufacturer in advanced materials and manufacturing. Recorded funding is about 2.1 billion Chinese yuan. Its products, customers and ownership are not confirmed here, though the sector suggests tanks, vessels and systems for storing and moving liquefied gases for industrial or energy users. B2B industrial brand with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

ITS Technology Group is a UK managed network and IT services provider, based in Chester, offering connectivity, cloud, managed IT and hosted telephony for public sector and business customers, and operating a dark-fibre network infrastructure across the north-west of England and North Wales. It serves schools, councils, health bodies and companies, and was supported by private equity investors. Recorded funding is about 247 million. B2B telecom brand with little consumer awareness.

MAHLE is a German automotive supplier headquartered in Stuttgart, producing pistons, engine components, filtration, thermal management and air-conditioning systems, and mechatronic parts for combustion and electric vehicles. Customers are car and truck makers and the aftermarket, with revenue of around 12 billion euros and about 70,000 employees. It is owned by the MAHLE Foundation. Privately held. B2B brand known in motorsport circles through sponsorship, including a history in Formula 1 engine technology, with little consumer awareness.

Mobvista is a Chinese mobile advertising technology company with global headquarters shown as Singapore, founded in Guangzhou, which offers a mobile ad network, Mintegral, programmatic advertising (Mobvista), analytics and app monetisation to app and game developers. Revenue is mostly in billions of yuan from advertisers. It is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (1860), and is known for its Mintegral and Mobvista (renamed Mobvista Group, 2022) services. B2B ad tech brand with no consumer awareness.

Photonic Inc. is a Coquitlam, British Columbia quantum technology company building a distributed, silicon-based quantum computing architecture linked by photons, founded in 2016, with strategic investors including Microsoft, with whom it has a partnership on quantum networking. It raised about 318 million dollars, and is privately held. Customers would be enterprises, governments and research bodies using future quantum computers. Research-stage technology brand with no consumer awareness.

Puttshack is an upscale entertainment venue company operating indoor mini-golf venues with ball-tracking technology that scores play automatically, alongside bars, cocktails and food. It started in London in 2018 and has expanded to venues in the UK and US, with a Chicago base shown for its US business. Recorded funding is about 292 million dollars. Consumer entertainment brand aimed at groups and corporate events, with growing awareness in major cities.

Saratoga Investment Corp is a New York-based business development company (BDC) that provides senior secured loans to US middle-market companies, managed by Saratoga Investment Advisors. It makes money from interest and fees on its credit portfolio, and pays dividends to shareholders. It is listed on the NYSE (SAR). Recorded funding of about 298 million dollars. Financial brand with little public awareness outside income investors.

TETRA Technologies is a Spring, Texas energy services and chemicals company that provides calcium chloride, completion fluids and water management for oil and gas operators, plus lithium and bromine development in Arkansas, and Deepwater production support. Customers are oil and gas operators and industrial users, with revenue of about 600 million dollars. It is listed on the NYSE (TTI). B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness.

Aspect Biosystems is a Vancouver biotechnology company that uses 3D bioprinting to develop tissue therapeutics, including bioprinted cell therapies for diabetes, which are being developed with Novo Nordisk in a deal worth up to 2.6 billion dollars announced in 2023. It has raised about 253 million dollars, including a 115 million dollar round in 2025. Privately held. Research-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

Atomic Machines is an Emeryville, California deep-tech company developing atomic-scale manufacturing technology for MEMS, semiconductors and nano devices, with ambitions to build precise structures atom by atom. Recorded funding is about 250 million dollars, though this figure looks high for a startup at its stage. Customers would be chipmakers and advanced manufacturers. Privately held. Early-stage technology brand with no consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cap Hill Brands is a Seattle-based consumer products company that invests in and builds brands in categories such as pain relief, oral care and wellness, selling to consumers via retail and e-commerce. Recorded funding is about 250 million dollars. Privately held. Consumer goods brand owner, with its individual products more visible than the parent. Product list and scale are not confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Farther is a New York-based wealth management platform, a registered investment adviser that uses technology and advisers to serve affluent households with investing, planning and tax advice. Customers are high-net-worth individuals, and revenue comes from advisory fees on managed assets, reportedly more than 8 billion dollars. It has raised about 268 million dollars. Privately held. Finance brand with modest awareness among affluent clients.

GOOD Meat is a San Francisco-based cultivated meat company, a division of Eat Just, which makes cultured chicken grown from animal cells, and was the first to win regulatory approval for sale, in Singapore in 2020 and in the US in 2023. Its products are sold in a few restaurants and, in Singapore, in retail as a blended product. Recorded funding is about 267 million dollars. Privately held. Early stage consumer food brand, with scaled-back operations since 2023.

MariaDB is an open-source relational database company, with a US base in Milpitas, California, and origins in Finland, created by the original MySQL founders. It sells MariaDB Enterprise Server, SkySQL cloud database service and related tools to businesses and cloud customers. It went public on the NYSE through a SPAC in 2022 (MRDB), and was taken private by K1 Investment Management in 2024. B2B software brand, known to developers, with no consumer awareness.

Savant Wealth Management is a Rockford, Illinois registered investment adviser, offering investment management, financial planning, tax and retirement plan services to individuals, families and businesses, through offices across the US. It manages more than 20 billion dollars of assets and has grown through acquisitions of local advisory firms. It is backed by private equity. Recorded funding is about 270 million dollars. Finance brand with strong regional visibility in the Midwest.

Stealth Communications is a New York City-based fibre internet and telecom provider, offering high-speed fibre broadband, dark fibre and connectivity to apartment buildings, businesses and carriers in New York and some other US cities. Founded in 2007, it has recorded funding of about 280 million dollars. Privately held. It serves both business and residential customers, with modest awareness in New York and little national profile.

Tembici is a Brazilian micromobility company based in Sao Paulo, which runs bike-sharing systems in cities including Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Santiago, Buenos Aires and Salvador, under local names like Bike Itau, and provides last-mile delivery fleets for e-commerce. Customers are commuters and city governments and corporate sponsors, and Itau is the main naming sponsor. Recorded funding is about 267 million dollars. Privately held. Recognised urban mobility brand in Brazil.

Xingji Meizu Group is a Chinese consumer electronics and smart device company based in Wuhan, Hubei, connected to the Meizu smartphone brand, which is now controlled by Geely's Xingji Era group. It develops a platform of full-stack smart terminals and in-car or wearable systems, linking phones, vehicles and smart devices. Recorded funding is about 2 billion yuan. Meizu is a known phone brand in China. Details of its current group structure are not fully confirmed here.

Harmonic is a San Jose, California video delivery and broadband technology company, selling video processing and delivery software, a cloud-native streaming platform (VOS360), and cable broadband access gear (CableOS) to broadcasters, streaming services and cable operators. Customers include Comcast, Charter and global broadcasters. Revenue is around 700 million dollars. Founded in 1988, it is listed on Nasdaq (HLIT). B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness, though its tech supports live sports streaming.

Beckett Collectibles is a Plano, Texas-based company that publishes price guides for sports cards and collectibles, operates a grading service (Beckett Grading Services), and runs an online marketplace and magazines. It is known as the standard for sports trading card values. Customers are collectors and dealers. Privately held, with recorded funding of 235 million dollars. Strong brand in the sports card hobby, with sports-fan reach.

BitDAO was a decentralised autonomous organisation based in Panama that raised about 230 million dollars from backers including Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, run by token holders and supported by the crypto exchange Bybit. It funded crypto and blockchain projects, and in 2023 merged with Mantle to form Mantle Network (MNT token), an Ethereum layer-2 scaling system. Crypto-sector brand, with no real consumer awareness beyond the crypto community.

CODA Automotive was a Los Angeles electric vehicle and battery company that sold the CODA sedan, a small all-electric car using a lithium-iron-phosphate battery, from 2012. It raised about 229 million dollars but filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2013 and later restructured as Mullen Technologies, then Mullen Automotive. It was a niche US EV brand with low sales and has no remaining standalone business.

Seek Pet Foods is a Chinese pet food manufacturer based in Linyi, Shandong, working on an OEM and ODM basis for dog and cat food brands and also producing its own products. Recorded funding is about 1.57 billion yuan. Customers are pet brands and retailers in China and exports. Its ownership and scale are not confirmed here. B2B manufacturer with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Brite Energy Partners is a South Korean clean energy company based in Seoul, developing a platform and app-based services for solar power, aggregation and renewable energy trading for homes and businesses. Recorded funding is about 276 billion won. Its customers, ownership and scale are not confirmed here. Clean energy technology brand with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Castor Maritime is a Limassol, Cyprus shipping company, listed on Nasdaq (CTRM), which owns and operates dry bulk vessels carrying iron ore, coal and grain, and has expanded into other businesses via its investment in Toro Corp and in MPC Container Ships. Controlled by Petros Panagiotidis. Customers are commodity traders and charterers. Recorded funding is about 211 million dollars. B2B shipping brand with no consumer awareness.

DICE is a London-based music ticketing platform and app, founded in 2014 by Phil Hutcheon, which sells tickets to gigs, club nights and festivals, with a focus on fans' access and fair pricing. It has operations in the UK, US and Europe, and raised about 200 million dollars from investors. Privately held. Consumer ticketing app with strong appeal to young music audiences and a growing live events footprint.

Gnosis is a blockchain infrastructure company, registered in Gibraltar, building decentralised tools on Ethereum including Gnosis Chain, Safe (formerly Gnosis Safe) multi-signature wallets, CoW Protocol, and Zodiac. It started in 2015 with prediction markets and raised money through a 2017 token sale, with funding recorded at about 212 million dollars. The GNO token governs the ecosystem. Crypto-sector brand with no consumer awareness beyond blockchain users.

Kazyon is Egypt's largest discount supermarket chain, based in Cairo, with hundreds of stores selling groceries and household goods at low prices to Egyptian consumers. It is backed by private investors and has recorded funding of about 215 million dollars. Privately held. Mass-market consumer retail brand in Egypt with good local awareness, and a shop footprint across many governorates that offers wide reach.

National Supercomputing Centre (NSCC) Singapore is the government-backed organisation managing Singapore's national supercomputing facilities, set up in 2015. It gives high-performance computing resources to researchers, universities, public agencies and industry, with a petascale system and the larger ASPIRE 2A system. Funding recorded is about 270 million Singapore dollars. State-supported. Research infrastructure brand with no consumer awareness, though it is known in science and technology circles.

SkyCell is a Zurich-based pharmaceutical logistics company that develops temperature-controlled shipping containers for transporting vaccines, biologics and other medicines by air and road, and sells container leasing with data monitoring. Customers are pharma firms and logistics providers worldwide. Founded in 2012, it has raised about 215 million dollars from investors including Hillhouse. Privately held. B2B healthcare logistics brand, known in pharma supply chains.

Summit Wash Holdings is described as a membership-focused car wash company based in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, classified in retail. Recorded funding is about 200 million dollars. Its brands, number of sites, ownership and scale are not confirmed here, though the sector points to subscription-based express exterior washes for local drivers. Likely a regional consumer service with local visibility only. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Superdry is a British clothing brand based in Cheltenham, founded in 2003 by Julian Dunkerton and James Holder, selling casual and outdoor fashion with Japanese-inspired graphics, through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale partners in over 60 countries. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange (SDRY) until delisted in 2024 after a restructuring that made it privately owned by Julian Dunkerton. Recorded funding is about 218 million dollars. Recognisable high-street consumer brand, though declining in the UK.

Temenos is a Geneva-based Swiss banking software company that supplies core banking, payments, digital banking, wealth management and fund administration software, such as Temenos Transact and Infinity, to banks in over 150 countries. Customers include retail banks, challenger banks and neo-banks, with revenue of about 1 billion dollars. Founded in 1993, it is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (TEMN). B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

Universal Technical Institute (UTI) is a Phoenix, Arizona-based for-profit education company that runs technical training schools for automotive, diesel, motorcycle, collision repair, marine, welding and HVAC careers, with about 16 campuses in the US under UTI, MMI and NASCAR Technical Institute. Students are high school graduates and career changers, with revenue of about 800 million dollars. Founded in 1965, it is listed on the NYSE (UTI). Familiar US vocational brand, with a long motorsport association.

Unizen is a Liechtenstein-based digital asset trading platform, based in Vaduz, that aggregates liquidity from decentralised and centralised exchanges and offers a unified swap and trading interface, together with its UZN token.
